Agent.description: A portable abstract agent role declaration.

id.description: Role identifier, referenced by sequence items as `agent:<id>`.

session.description:
Optional session binding for this agent's frames: `session:<id>`
(shared with every other agent bound to the same declared session),
or a bare `per-frame`/`persistent` lifecycle value, which is always
agent-local and never implies sharing. Omitted preserves legacy
configuration-driven behavior during migration; absent both canonical
and configured values remains `per-frame`.

system.description:
Optional standing instructions for this role, delivered through the
harness's system-prompt channel once per session rather than repeated
in every frame's user message. Holds doctrine the role always obeys —
not per-step work, which belongs in the step's own prompt. Model-visible
like any other instruction text: compiled into the model view, audited
for hidden content, and covered by the canonical digest.

BranchFailureEntry.description:
One ordered `branch-failure` entry naming a declared branch and its
terminal failure policy.

oneOf.description:
Discard the branch's uncommitted effects and continue the panel with
the remaining branches.
Leave the run in a clean, resumable blocked state. Never escalates.

Discard all uncommitted panel effects and route through the panel's
own `on-failure`, or escalate exactly like any other control kind's
unrouted failure. The default for an unlisted branch.

ChecklistItem.description:
One declared checklist item: the unit that receives exactly one verdict.

`id` is the item's identity and is stable across rewordings of `text` — a
reworded criterion keeps its id and changes its digest, which is what lets
a receipt distinguish "this item was answered again" from "this item now
asks something else". Deriving an id from `text` would collapse that
distinction, so ids are declared, never computed.

detail.description:
Elaboration presented alongside `text`. Detail is never separately
verdict-bearing: one item is one verdict.

id.description: Item identifier, unique within its checklist.

requires-evidence.description:
Whether a verdict for this item must carry evidence. When any item in
a checklist requires it, the synthesized verdict schema makes the
`evidence` field required.

text.description: The criterion as the reviewer reads it.

CommandDeclaration.description:
Advanced command declaration table. The source shorthand `cmd = "..."`
remains the primary authoring path; this table carries explicit argv when
the author needs to avoid string parsing entirely.

argv-from.description:
Local `[schema:text]` input port resolved once into concrete argv when
the command frame is built. Slots are deliberately unsupported so an
agent-produced value cannot select the executable.

success-exit-code.description: Exit codes treated as success. Defaults to `[0]` semantically.

CompositionRefList.description:
Scalar-or-array string list for composition typed refs.

Authoring accepts a string or an array of strings; canonical serialization
is always an array.

Condition.description: A named condition body keyed by `[condition.<id>]`.

ConditionMap.description: Duplicate-aware map of named conditions keyed by condition ID.

Conflicts.description:
A `[[relations.conflicts]]` entry: targetless — applies to the declaring
trait when `when` matches. Rejects `target`, `required`, `suggested`,
`conflicting`, `strength`, `max-depth`, `follows`, and `suppresses`.

conflict.description:
Traits or behavior axes that should not co-activate.
Accepted ref kinds: `trait`, `behavior`.

conflict-policy.description:
What to do when conflicts are found: `require-decision`,
`warn-and-isolate`, `fail-plan`.

merge-strategy.description: How to combine with other traits: `structured`, `isolated`, `render-only`.

ContractRefList.description:
Normalized list of contract ref strings for prompt input/output fields.
Accepts scalar-or-array at the decode boundary but always stores a
`Vec<String>` — source scalar-vs-array shape is not preserved as semantic
state. This type is distinct from [`TargetList`](crate::shared::TargetList)
so render target lists and protocol contract refs cannot drift together.

manual.description: Manual activation is declarative data only; later phases gate runtime use.

rule.description: Ordered rules. Rules compose as OR during scoring.

Dependency.description:
A dependency declaration: alias, trait identity, version, and optional
source metadata.

alias.description:
Typed reference namespace for this dependency (e.g. `"aws"`).

Must be unique within the manifest. Used to qualify refs such as
`slot:aws/scope`. Must be a single-segment namespace without `:`, `.`,
`/`, or whitespace.

id.description: The trait ID being depended on (e.g. `"ctx/aws-log-primitives"`).

source.description:
Optional source metadata. When omitted, the source must be resolved
from the package-local `trait.lock` or provided explicitly by the caller.

Digest.description: A typed digest value in `sha256:<hex>` format.

Eval.description:
An `[[eval]]` declaration: a declared product evaluation check.

Eval declarations describe checks that can be run against a trait. They do
not execute by themselves. The `input` and `output` fields are product
refs (e.g. `render:agent-skills`, `fixture:fixtures/example.md`,
`trait:self`, `report:scenario-shape`), not repository test fixtures.

output.description:
Expected fixture, report, or comparison output (e.g.
`fixture:fixtures/example.md`, `report:scenario-shape`).

scenario.description:
Scenario IDs this eval covers (references to `[[scenario]]` IDs).

Canonical authoring uses singular `scenario` (scalar-or-array):
`scenario = "happy-path"` or
`scenario = ["happy-path", "edge-case"]`.

EvalVariant.description:
The variant of an eval declaration.

MVP variants (`documentation`, `lint`, `golden-render`) have initial
implementation paths. Future variants (`behavioral`, `runtime`) are
declared but may be unsupported for execution.

oneOf.description: Documentation completeness or accuracy check.
Static lint or structural check.
Golden-file render comparison.
Behavioral check (future harness).
Runtime check (future harness).

ExhaustionTarget.description:
A loop's `on-exhausted` declaration: the keywords `"continue"`/`"abort"`,
or one or more signal refs emitted when the loop continues past
exhaustion. A one-element sequence collapses to `One` on decode so each
meaning has exactly one canonical spelling.

FailureTarget.description:
A control failure either emits a legacy signal or abandons the current path
and schedules a later top-level recovery step.

GuardExpr.description:
One guard expression. A string ref is either `signal:<id>` or
`condition:<id>`. An array is OR/any composition.

elapsed-seconds-at-least.description:
Cumulative active-drive elapsed seconds (runtime-supplied evidence,
never a core wall clock) at least this threshold. Threshold is a JSON
number or a `{ ref = "slot:..."/"port:..." }` numeric reference.

field-equals.description:
Filters `count` to elements whose `field` equals this value. Paired
with `field`; meaningless alone. Kept distinct from `equals`, which is
already the count's threshold — one predicate needs both a "which
elements" and a "how many", and they cannot share a spelling.

present.description:
Presence-aware leaf (schema-version `"0.3"` only). Bare form is a local
optional input `port:*`; with `field`, a declared optional field of a
local `port:*`/`slot:*` object container. Yields `Matched`/`NotMatched`/`Unmeasurable`
tri-state internally; only `Matched` routes `true`.

GuidanceItem.description: A slug-identified guidance item with optional local render text.

GuidanceItemList.description: Scalar-or-array guidance list. Strings normalize to slug-only items.

Id.description:
Stable, durable trait identifier (not a display name).

Must be non-empty and use only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.
Display names and search labels are separate fields.

JoinPolicy.description:
Closed, policy-discriminated barrier join for a `parallel` sequence item.
Omission on `SequenceItem.join` is behaviorally identical to
`{ policy = "collect-in-order" }` — the P263 barrier.

oneOf.description:
Every branch's own effects merge into the enclosing target in authored
order. Exact P263 barrier behavior.

Fold each committed branch's `source` slot value, in authored order,
into one panel-owned `destination` slot using `merge`/`set-field`
write-operation semantics. `append`/`replace`/`increment` are rejected.

Collect each committed branch's `source` slot value, in authored
order, into a panel-owned list-typed `destination` slot, then evaluate
`guard` against the committed ledger. A false guard is a failed
quorum.

Metadata.description:
`[metadata]` facets: family, variant, job, domain, artifact, audience,
environment, tag.

All facets use kebab-case slug strings with scalar-or-array authoring.
Slug validation happens in the post-decode taxonomy pass. `family` and
`variant` are display-only: they never drive activation or canonical
trait resolution. Since P451, a declared `variant` additionally selects
which `[agent.variant.<v>.role.*]` config qualifier a run resolves
against (config routing, not activation or canonical resolution — see
`ctx_traits_io::harness_config::resolve_run_variant`).

family.description:
Declared family identity for list grouping and consistency
advisories against the trait package ID. Display-only.

Name.description: Human-readable display name, not a durable identifier.

NamedSequence.description: A named sequence block keyed by `[sequence.<id>]`.

description.description: Human-readable description of the sequence block.

sequence.description: Ordered items in this sequence block.

NamedSequenceMap.description: Duplicate-aware map of named sequences keyed by sequence ID.

OutputSink.description:
A step output sink.

Existing manifests serialize a plain typed ref string. New authoring may use
an inline table for slot write operations, e.g.
`{ slot = "slot:notes", operation = "append" }`.

OutputSinkList.description: Normalized list of sequence output sinks.

default.description:
Optional runtime default source for input ports. Static render/check do
not execute it; CLI/IO runtime may use it only with explicit permission.

direction.description: Whether this is an input or output port.

optional.description: Whether this port is optional. Defaults to `false`.

value.description:
For output ports: the slot ref that exposes the value (`"slot:<id>"`).
Input ports must not declare `value`.

PortDefault.description: Runtime default source for an input port.

PortDefaultCommand.description: Command-backed runtime default source for an input port.

capture-bytes.description:
Runtime stdout capture ceiling in bytes. Absent uses the IO host's
documented default-input capture ceiling. A capture that exceeds this
fails the run rather than landing a truncated value in the port.

timeout-ms.description:
Runtime timeout in milliseconds. Absent uses the IO host's documented
default-input timeout.

PredicateList.description:
Scalar-or-array string list for activation predicates.

Authoring accepts either a string or an array of strings; canonical
serialization is always an array.

Procedure.description:
A `[procedure]` section: deterministic sequence orchestration.

Optional top-level section. When present, `description` must be non-empty
and `sequence` must be non-empty. The `input` and `output` contract fields
declare procedure-level boundary ports. `sequence` holds inline
`[[procedure.sequence]]` items; `sequence-order` optionally reorders them.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the procedure accomplishes.

sequence.description:
Ordered `[[procedure.sequence]]` items. Definition order is the default
execution order unless `sequence-order` is present.

sequence-order.description:
Optional explicit ordering of sequence item IDs. If present, every
sequence item must have a unique ID, every listed ID must exist,
duplicate IDs are invalid, and unlisted items are invalid.

worktree-required.description:
Require prepared worktree provenance before the procedure can expose
its first prompt or command frame.

ProcedureRefList.description:
Normalized list of ref strings for procedure `input`, `output`, and
`sequence` fields.

Accepts scalar-or-array at the decode boundary but always stores a
`Vec<String>`. Distinct from
[`ContractRefList`](crate::trait::prompt::ContractRefList) so procedure
contracts remain independent.

Projection.description:
One ordered write in a closed `project` sequence item.

Runtime reads every slot source from one pre-step snapshot, optionally
selects one top-level object field, validates every destination write,
then commits all writes atomically. A literal source (P431) is a canonical
value declared on the projection itself rather than read from a slot;
literal-backed projections contribute no sequence input and reject
`field`. Destinations are local typed slots; `replace`, `append`, and
`increment` are the supported operations.

ProjectionSource.description:
One `procedure.sequence[].projection[].source`: either an existing local
slot ref, or a canonical typed literal wrapped as `{ literal = <value> }`.
The wrapper keeps the literal form unambiguous with the plain string
slot-ref shape — an unwrapped string literal would be indistinguishable
from `source = "slot:..."`.

Prompt.description:
A `[prompt.<id>]` body: inline text or resource source plus contracts.

The prompt ID is the map key in `Trait.prompts`, not a field on this
struct.

input.description:
Required input refs for this prompt (e.g. `port:user-prompt`,
`slot:scope`, `resource:checklist`). Accepts scalar-or-array,
normalized to a flat list.

output.description:
Output contract refs — local `slot:<id>` refs only. Accepts
scalar-or-array, normalized to a flat list.

text.description:
The prompt body text. May contain typed ref interpolations like
`{port:user-prompt}` or `{slot:scope}`.

PromptMap.description:
A map of prompt IDs to prompt bodies that rejects duplicate keys at decode
time rather than silently overwriting.

This wraps [`BTreeMap<String, Prompt>`] with a custom `Deserialize` that
detects duplicate keys and returns an error before collapsing them.

Reference.description:
A parsed canonical typed reference: `<kind>:<path>`.

The path is preserved verbatim from the source text. [`Self::ref_path`]
decomposes it into namespace and id for dependency-qualified refs.
`Display` round-trips to the canonical accepted text.

RelationsRefList.description: Scalar-or-array typed reference list for `when` conditions.

Requires.description: A `[[relations.requires]]` entry: the source needs the target.

when.description:
Conditions that enable this relation: `rule:*` or `signal:*` refs.
Entries in one `when` list are AND; multiple entries model OR.

Resource.description:
An `[[resource]]` declaration: an external blob reference or inline text.

File-backed resources are materialized from IO evidence. Inline content is
materialized entirely within core without filesystem access.

content.description: Inline resource body. Inline resources require no host IO.

digest.description:
Canonical pin over the resource's expected file bytes, in
`sha256:<hex>` form. Presence marks this resource protected: IO must
verify actual bytes against this pin immediately before the resource
reaches a model or a command spawns, and `ctx traits check` reports
drift between this pin and the file on disk. Valid only on a
path-backed resource — inline and checklist bodies are already
canonical bytes with no filesystem path to verify. Omitted from
canonical serialization when absent, so every existing unpinned
declaration stays byte-identical. Adding or changing this pin changes
`Resource`'s canonical digest, which is how pinning or repinning a
resource moves the trait's machine-trust decision to stale.

hint.description: Advisory hint about the resource contents or usage.

input.description: Typed inputs required by a resource template.

item.description:
Declared checklist items. Valid only alongside `variant = "checklist"`,
where they replace `path`/`content` as the resource body: the items are
canonical and the presented text is rendered from them, so no prose
copy of the checklist can drift from the typed one.

path.description: Path to the resource blob, relative to `root`.

render.description:
How this resource's body is presented to the model. Defaults to
`reference` for path-backed resources and `inline` for content or
checklist resources (see `effective_render()`); omitted from
canonical serialization when unset, so existing declarations stay
byte-identical.

root.description:
Which root the declared `path` is relative to. Defaults to `package`
and is omitted from canonical serialization when default, so existing
package-relative declarations stay byte-identical.

trigger.description: When to load the resource at runtime.

variant.description: Optional resource kind. `template` resources may declare typed inputs.

ResourceInputList.description: Normalized typed-ref inputs for resource templates.

ResourceRender.description:
How a resource's body reaches the model: presented as an openable file
reference or embedded inline in model-visible output.

This is a separate axis from `trigger` (when a resource loads) and from
`path`/`content` (where its body comes from). A `path`-backed resource may
still declare `render = "inline"` to have its file body read at the IO
edge and embedded, exactly as a `content` resource is embedded today.

oneOf.description: Presented as an openable file reference; bytes stay on disk.
Embedded verbatim in model-visible output.

ResourceRoot.description:
Where a resource's declared path is rooted.

`Package` (the default, and omitted from canonical serialization) resolves
against the trait package directory, jailed as today. `Repo` resolves
against the invocation repository root discovered at the IO boundary —
repo-root resources are repo-coupled and not portable across checkouts.

oneOf.description: The trait package directory (default).
The invocation repository root.

ResourceTrigger.description: When a resource is needed at runtime.

oneOf.description: Loaded when the trait is activated.
Loaded when the first step that needs it is reached.

id.description: Stable rule ID. Required and unique within `[activation]`.

reason.description: Human-readable reason shown by explanation surfaces.

Scenario.description:
A `[[scenario]]` declaration: a product review behavior example.

Scenarios are behavior hints/specifications for humans, renderers, lint
checks, prompt review, and future behavioral eval harnesses. They are not
proof by themselves.

output.description: Expected result, refusal, warning, or behavior description.

tag.description:
Optional advisory tags for filtering or grouping.

Canonical authoring uses singular `tag` (scalar-or-array):
`tag = "security"` or `tag = ["security", "rust"]`.

variant.description: Behavior variant: positive, negative, or edge.

ScenarioVariant.description: The behavioral variant of a scenario.

oneOf.description: Expected to work correctly.
Expected to fail, refuse, or warn.
Boundary condition or unusual input.

SchemaDeclaration.description:
A `[[schema]]` declaration: a named schema contract.

Must have exactly one of `resource`, `fields`, or scalar `schema`.

allowed.description: Closed set of allowed scalar values for scalar enum schemas.

fields.description:
Inline field declarations for duck-typed compatibility.
Mutually exclusive with `resource`.

resource.description:
Resource ref: `resource:<id>` pointing to an opaque blob.
Mutually exclusive with `fields`.

schema.description:
Scalar schema ref for closed-value enum schemas.
Mutually exclusive with `resource` and `fields`.

SchemaField.description: One inline field declaration for duck-typed schema compatibility.

allowed.description: Optional closed set of allowed scalar values for this field.

anyOf.description:
A slot input that never gates validation, planning, recovery, or
runtime readiness (P447). Omitted from the frame entirely when no
accepted value exists; presented through the normal available-input
path once one does.

SequenceInput.description:
One `procedure.sequence[].input` entry.

An ordinary entry is a plain typed ref string (`port:*`, `slot:*`,
`resource:*`). A resource ref may additionally carry a `when` guard,
authored as `{ ref = "resource:<id>", when = <GuardExpr> }`; the runtime
includes that resource in the step's available context and
`resource_evidence` only when the guard matches at readiness. A slot ref
may instead be authored as `{ slot = "slot:<id>", optional = true }`
(P447): that slot never gates validation, planning, recovery, or runtime
readiness, and is omitted from the frame entirely until an accepted value
exists. Port inputs and plain (non-decorated) slot inputs remain
unconditional.

SequenceInputList.description:
Normalized list of `procedure.sequence[].input` entries.

Accepts scalar-or-array at the decode boundary, where each element is a
plain ref string, a guarded-resource table, or an optional-slot table
(P447). Always stores a `Vec<SequenceInput>`.

SequenceItem.description:
A `[[procedure.sequence]]` item: one item in the procedure, owned by the
procedure rather than by a separate top-level table.

`[[procedure.sequence]]` definition order is the default execution order.
An optional `id` allows `procedure.sequence-order` to customize ordering.

agent.description: Optional abstract agent role that should serve this executable item.

branch-failure.description:
`parallel` ordered per-branch terminal failure policy. A branch with
no entry defaults to `panel-fail`.

branches.description:
Ordered, author-order list of local `sequence:<id>` refs run as
independent branches of a `kind = "parallel"` item. Never sorted.

cmd.description: Simple no-shell command shorthand for a command-backed sequence item.

command.description:
Explicit command declaration. `cmd` and `command` are mutually
exclusive source forms and lower to the same command plan.

concurrent.description:
`for-each` concurrency request. Additive: `false`/absent is byte-identical
to documents authored before concurrency existed.

format.description: Optional format preferences. Accepted as a format-preference declaration on prompt/command items; rejected on control items.

id.description: Optional stable identifier for sequence-order references.

input.description:
Input refs (e.g. `port:user-prompt`, `slot:scope`, `resource:data`).
A resource entry may additionally be authored as a guarded table
(`{ ref = "resource:<id>", when = <GuardExpr> }`); the runtime
includes it in this step's frame only when the guard matches.

join.description:
`parallel` barrier join policy. Omitted is behaviorally identical to
`{ policy = "collect-in-order" }` (P263 barrier).

kind.description:
Explicit item kind. When omitted, `prompt`, `cmd`, and `command` fields
provide the current authoring sugar for prompt/command inference.

max-branches.description:
Required positive upper bound on `branches` length for a `parallel`
item. `branches.len()` must not exceed this bound.

max-iterations-from.description:
Local `schema:integer` input port resolved once at loop entry and frozen
into the runtime control frame. Mutually exclusive with
`max-iterations`.

on-abort.description:
Names the signal(s) to emit when `abort-if` is the arm that halts the
loop, so the trait's own terminal reason (e.g.
`recurring-blocker-unresolved`) is distinguishable from exhaustion in
the ledger, the receipt, and `run-status` — the runtime still reports
the accurate mechanism (`abort-if-matched`) alongside it. Requires
`abort-if`; the `"continue"`/`"abort"` keywords are meaningless here
(an `abort-if` match always halts the loop) and are rejected.

on-complete.description:
Declared signal refs this item may emit, either directly as refs or
derived from deterministic output predicates. On a for-each item this
is instead the completion signal, emitted once (at most one entry
allowed there).

on-exhausted.description:
Loop exhaustion policy: `"continue"` (the default when omitted),
`"abort"`, or one or more `signal:<id>` refs.

Continuing treats exhaustion as a normal outcome — the sequence
proceeds to the next item, and any declared signals are emitted as
recorded evidence a later guard may read (or ignore). Spending a
bounded budget without matching `until` means the work is unfinished,
which the following step is responsible for reading; it does not mean
the run is broken.

`"abort"` stops the run at exhaustion, for procedures where an unmet
exit condition invalidates every step after the loop; no signal is
emitted in that case. A run started with strict loops aborts every
loop regardless of its declared policy, and suppresses signal
emission even when the declaration names one.

on-failure.description: Legacy failure signal or structured forward recovery route.

otherwise.description: Optional named sequence ref selected when a branch guard is false.

projection.description:
Ordered deterministic writes for `kind = "project"`. All source values
are read before any destination is committed.

prompt.description: Prompt ref (`prompt:<id>`) or inline prompt text.

sequence.description: Named sequence ref (`sequence:<id>`) for sequence/loop/for-each items.

success-exit-code.description: Exit codes treated as success for simple `cmd` shorthand.

timeout-ms.description: Runtime timeout in milliseconds for simple `cmd` shorthand.

title.description: Human-readable title for this sequence step.

when.description: Branch entry guard. A true guard selects `sequence`.

SequenceKind.description: Sequence item kind. Omitted kind infers prompt or command from authored fields.

oneOf.description: A human-owned prompt frame resumed through the ordinary output path.

Deterministic, runtime-owned slot projection. It never creates an agent
or command frame.

Session.description: A `[[session]]` declaration: a named, shareable session identity.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of what this session is for.

id.description: Session identifier, referenced by agents as `session:<id>`.

Signal.description: A `[[signal]]` declaration: a named event identity.

description.description: Human-readable description of when this signal fires.

SignalEmissionRule.description: A signal ref or a deterministic signal derivation rule.

Slot.description: A `[[slot]]` definition: a procedure run ledger value contract.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this slot represents.

hint.description:
Advisory hint for the expected slot value, examples, or constraints
useful to a step prompt. Metadata only — schema remains the validation
contract.

Slug.description:
A kebab-case slug: lowercase letters/digits separated by single hyphens.

Deserializes permissively (raw string). Validation happens through
explicit construction (`Slug::new`, `Slug::new_at`) or the post-decode
taxonomy validation pass (`Slug::check`). Custom user slugs are allowed
when syntactically valid; no built-in vocabulary table is enforced.

SlugList.description:
Kebab-case slug list: accepts scalar-or-array input and normalizes to
`Vec<Slug>`.

Always serializes as an array (canonical output). Slug shape validation
happens in the post-decode taxonomy pass, not during deserialization, so
diagnostics carry canonical field paths.

Suggests.description: A `[[relations.suggests]]` entry: advisory influence toward target.

WriteOperation.description: Runtime write operation for a slot output sink.

oneOf.description: Replace the slot value with the supplied output value.
Append the supplied output element to an array slot.
Deep-merge the supplied object delta into an object slot.
Write the supplied output value to one named object field.
Add the supplied numeric delta to a number slot.

description:
The canonical trait root aggregate: identity, guidance, activation, ports,
slots, schemas, signals, prompts, procedure, composition, and relations.

activation.description:
Declaration matching declarations. Pure data only; runtime activation is
resolved by later gated phases.

agent.description: Declared abstract agent roles for multi-harness procedure routing.

behavior.description: Behavior: how the trait should act.

composition.description:
Contract contract: conflict declarations and merge policy.
Pure data only; runtime composition planning is separate.

dependency.description:
Dependencies that this trait references by alias, e.g.
`resource:aws/rubric`. Resolution is performed at the IO/check boundary.

eval.description: Product eval declarations: declared checks that can be run.

intent.description: Intent: what the trait requires, focuses on, avoids, and blocks.

metadata.description: Searchable metadata facets. Separate from activation.

port.description: Port declarations: boundary contracts for trait dataflow.

prompt.description:
Prompt definitions: reusable prompt bodies with optional contracts.
Map key is the prompt ID (TOML `[prompt.<id>]`).

relations.description:
Canonical relations: trait-to-trait requires, suggests, and targetless
conflicts. Pure data only; graph construction and evaluation are
separate deterministic passes.

resource.description:
Resource declarations: opaque blob references for schema bodies and
external data.

scenario.description:
Product review scenarios: positive, negative, and edge behavior
examples. Not executable test cases.

schema.description:
Local schema declarations: named object schema contracts backed by
resource refs or inline fields.

session.description:
Declared session identities: named, shareable session bindings that
`[[agent]].session` references target.

signal.description: Declared signal identities for procedure sequence emission.

slot.description: Slot definitions: procedure run ledger value contracts.

variant.description:
Native family leaf identity. This is deliberately absent from 0.2
documents, preserving their encoded bytes and digest semantics.

title: Trait
